title: Ensure 'Access this computer from the network' is set to 'Administrators, Authenticated Users, ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS' (DC only)
objective: Audit CIS checkpoint 2.2.2: Ensure 'Access this computer from the network' is set to 'Administrators, Authenticated Users, ENTERPRISE DOMAIN CONTROLLERS' (DC only)

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

fields.name: audit_output
fields.description: Raw output from the audit command

steps.name: Run read-only audit script for SeNetworkLogonRight
steps.function: 1. Use read-only PowerShell to check if the host is a Domain Controller and query the current value of 'Access this computer from the network'. Emits ** PASS **, ** FAIL **, ** SKIP **, or ** ERROR **. changed_when: false; failed_when: rc not in [0, 1].

steps.name: Determine CIS status from audit script markers
steps.function: 2. Evaluate the output of step-01 to determine compliance. PASS if the script reported compliant value; FAIL if non-compliant; SKIP if not a domain controller; ERROR on any failure.

computations._cis_status: PASS if audit output contains '** PASS **', FAIL if it contains '** FAIL **', SKIP if it contains '** SKIP **', otherwise ERROR

steps.name: Store final audit result as cis_result
steps.function: 3. Store the final audit result in a variable named 'cis_result' using set_fact. Set cis_result to the overall compliance status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR) derived from the last requirement's status variable.

steps.name: Generate audit report
steps.function:
4. Create a task named 'Generate audit report' using debug msg with EXACTLY this format:
AUDIT REPORT — CIS 2.2.2
Reference: CIS Benchmark checkpoint 2.2.2
Then for each requirement: REQUIREMENT NN - {{ req_NN }}:
  With fields: Task, Command, Exit code, Data, Status (PASS/FAIL/SKIP/ERROR), Details.
End with OVERALL COMPLIANCE: section containing Result: {{{ cis_result }}}

steps.name: Emit compliance result
steps.function: Output the overall compliance status to the caller.

steps.name: Handle task failure
steps.function: Reached via rescue block on any unexpected task failure.

compliance_constraints: Use failed_when: false on all audit tasks (except set_fact, debug) so all checks complete and report status
If the audit targets a specific software/service (e.g., GDM, GNOME, sshd, httpd), FIRST check if it is installed. If NOT installed, report SKIP for all checks.
This is an AUDIT playbook — it MUST NOT make any changes to the system. All tasks must be read-only (shell commands, stat, slurp, command with check-only flags, etc.).
The audit script must be read-only: it may create a temporary export file for secedit but must remove it afterward and must not modify any system settings.
reference_procedure: Navigate to the UI Path articulated in the Remediation section and confirm it is set as prescribed.
